summary: The recurring OOMKill cycle in notification-service is best explained by H1 (confidence 0.72, medium): the in-memory TemplateCache introduced by dep-5402 (v3.8.0, 2026-03-21T00:00Z) accumulates heap without an evident bound, producing a ~24h sawtooth and three exit-137 restarts. The onset evidence is tight — the entire observable pre-deploy day is flat at ~47-50% (F21), the deploy bucket is the local minimum (F23), and the first sustained monotonic ramp starts in the very next bucket while CPU stays flat at ~24.9% (F22/F25/F26) — and the alternative Kafka-retention story (H2) is structurally contradicted because cfg-2410 (03-23T18:00Z) postdates two of the three OOMKills and no broker restart, reassignment, or partition/topic change is recorded (F33/F34/F35). Confidence is capped at medium because the unbounded-growth mechanism itself is asserted from a one-line deploy manifest, not from code, cardinality metadata, or heap/old-gen telemetry (F14/F15/F16/F24). Treat this as an identified origin with a named suspect change rather than a proven defect; rule out H2 empirically and verify the cache bound in code before closing.

ranked_hypotheses.title: In-memory TemplateCache added by dep-5402 grows unbounded until recurring OOM cycle
ranked_hypotheses.statement: notification-service v3.8.0 (dep-5402, 2026-03-21T00:00Z, 'Add in-memory template cache for email rendering', ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment) introduced an in-memory cache inside notification-service that retains entries without an evident bound. Heap grows monotonically under steady consume load (memory_pct ramps +5-6pp per 2h bucket, CPU unchanged, old-gen pressure and multi-second full GCs) until the container hits its limit and is OOMKilled; the abrupt memory drop is the restart and the cycle repeats each ~24h. This origin is specific to notification-service: it is the ONLY service in the metric set with a sawtooth ramp/reset (F32), and the other broker-sharers are flat (settlement-service F27-F31, order-service F11), so the driver is the service's own heap growth, not shared-broker volume.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5402 deploys notification-service v3.8.0 adding a ConcurrentHashMap template cache keyed by template+locale+userSegment; no rollback ever occurs

Before the deploy the memory series is flat at ~47-50% for the entire observable pre-deploy day with no trend; the 03-21T00:00Z deploy bucket is the local MINIMUM (transient dip consistent with restart/scale at deploy time)

The first sustained monotonically rising memory averages begin in the very first bucket after the deploy (20-min rise starts 00:20Z; 40-min first strictly-rising bucket 00:40Z), climbing unbroken to ~58.97% by 06:00Z
Growth is accumulation, not increased processing: memory ramps while cpu_pct stays flat at ~24.4-25.3 across the deploy and the ramp
Old-gen heap crosses 90% and full GCs lengthen to 1.6-8.2s, clustering in the ramp/peak windows — retained entries are not reclaimed
memory_pct sawtooths from ~48-50% to ~97-98% then drops abruptly to ~48%, three times (resets ~21T22:00, 22T22:00, 23T20:00)
Each cycle ends in an OOMKill (exit 137) at 03-21T22:59:50Z, 03-22T21:59:47Z and 03-23T19:59:21Z; the restart resets the container, closing the loop

Scope check: NO other service in the metric set exhibits a sawtooth — settlement-service is flat (49.15-50.75 avg, zero restarts, lag max 82) and auth-service is flat (51.16-53.17 avg, zero restarts), corroborating that the accumulation is local to notification-service's own heap rather than a shared-broker/volume effect

The very large short-lived consumer_lag spike accompanying each restart window is read as a symptom of the cycle (backlog that queued while the consumer was stalled during the ramp and around the restart), not as the driver — CPU-flat growth rules out throughput-driven growth

assumptions: The TemplateCache has no TTL/size bound/eviction policy: only the one-line deploy manifest exists (F14/F15) and no code or diff endpoint was reachable, so the unbounded-growth mechanism is asserted from the deploy description, not inspected.
The userSegment key dimension is high-cardinality (per-user/per-request) rather than a small enum; no cardinality or segment metadata is exposed anywhere (F16).

notification-service's container memory limit was unchanged in the window and no memory-limit telemetry exists (F18/F19); this is answered only negatively from exhaustive change inventory, so the constant-threshold claim is not directly established.

No metric can decompose memory_pct into old-gen vs young-gen or cache vs non-cache (heap_pct not found, F24), so the ramp cannot be proven to be cache allocation rather than ordinary JVM heap warm-up.
Pre-03-20 baseline is unobservable (F12), so an identical earlier cycle before the metrics window cannot be strictly excluded.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Kafka retention reduction (cfg-2410) forced a replay/backlog surge notification-service could not absorb
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The platform-team Kafka maintenance cfg-2410 (log.retention.ms 7d->3d at 2026-03-23T18:00Z) forced a replay/backlog surge dumped into notification-service, which it could not absorb, blowing up its heap and OOMKilling it ~2h20m after the change. Structural timings strongly constrain this: cfg-2410 postdates two of the three OOMKills, and the record documents no broker restart or partition reassignment, so it can at most explain the 03-23 episode via an undocumented mechanism.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2410 reduces Kafka log.retention.ms 7d->3d at 03-23T18:00Z — the only config change in the window
Retention/broker maintenance triggers a replay/backlog surge (pattern of HIST-104 / HIST-112)
notification-service sees a huge short-lived consumer_lag spike (03-23T18:00Z avg 810, max 18138)
Processing the surge drives heap to its limit and the container is OOMKilled (exit 137 at 19:59:21Z)

assumptions: A replay/lag surge can exhaust heap by itself — untested: kafka exposes no consumer_lag and messages_in_per_s was never pulled (F13).
The lag spike precedes the heap peak within the 03-23 window; 2h buckets cannot order the sub-hour sequence of lag vs heap threshold vs OOMKill.
The reported episode is specifically the 03-23 OOM rather than the whole recurring 24h pattern.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Chronic pre-existing cycle with cause outside the observable window
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The three OOMKills form a ~24h periodic cycle whose true origin lies before the earliest observable data (metrics 03-20, logs 03-21T03:00Z) — e.g. a cron-like bulk workload, an upstream batch producer, or a pre-existing leak — and both dep-5402 and cfg-2410 are coincidental to it.

causal_chain.claim: Three near-identical ~24h cycles with resets at 21T22:00, 22T22:00, 23T20:00 suggest a periodic driver rather than a one-off event
Observable data begins only 03-20 (metrics) / 03-21T03:00Z (logs), so the true onset and any driver before that date cannot be read
An out-of-window periodic workload/leak drives heap to the limit each cycle, producing the OOMKill and reset

assumptions: The cycle genuinely extends before 03-20 — unverified, and contradicted for the one full pre-deploy day we can observe, which is flat at ~48% (F21).
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: No change anywhere in the full-scope, exhaustive inventory except dep-5402 and cfg-2410 (F1/F2/F35/F36); the one observable pre-deploy day is completely flat with the first sustained ramp in the bucket immediately after dep-5402 (F21/F22/F23/F26); the only other services in the metric set are flat (F32). No reachable out-of-window driver remains, so this is unfalsifiable speculation rather than evidence, kept only because pre-03-20 data is genuinely unreachable.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Container memory limit / node pressure causing OOMKills not attributable to application heap growth
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The OOMKills are driven by a resource-limit or node-scheduling condition (limit too low, or a neighbor consuming node memory) rather than by notification-service's own demand.

causal_chain.claim: OOMKilled (exit 137) events occur on notification-service pods
A limit reduction or node memory pressure would cause kills independent of heap growth
Heap-growth symptoms (full GCs, sawtooth) are incidental to the kills

assumptions: A node-pressure or limit-change event not in the inventory contributed
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: No memory-limit or scheduling change exists in the window (F2 explicitly found none), and the memory curve shows genuine application-driven heap ramp with old-gen growth and increasingly long full GCs (F7, F10) — a signature of real heap accumulation, not a low limit or external node pressure. A shared-broker neighbor (order-service) is flat (F11), arguing against node-wide pressure.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Sibling consumer or producer on the shared Kafka broker drove message volume/size into notification-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A producer or sibling consumer sharing the Kafka broker (F3/F4: kafka is shared) changed behavior and drove message volume or payload size into notification-service, causing retention-driven heap growth.

causal_chain.claim: kafka is shared=true, owned by platform-team; notification-service consumes it
A producer/sibling changed volume or payload size
notification-service heap grows under the increased retention/message load, eventually OOM

assumptions: An unidentified producer or sibling consumer changed message volume or size — but no such producer/sibling is even enumerated (F4), and no deployment/config change exists for any other service (F1)
Message size/throughput actually increased (unmeasured)
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The only two changes in the entire window are dep-5402 (notification-service) and cfg-2410 (Kafka retention) — no producer or sibling service deployed or changed config (F1). The dependency graph exposes no producers or sibling consumers at all (F4), so this is unfalsifiable speculation rather than evidence.

facts.statement: notification-service memory_pct shows a repeating sawtooth 2026-03-21 to 2026-03-23: baseline ~48-50%, steady ramp of ~+5-6pp per 2h bucket to ~97-98%, then abrupt drop back to ~48%, three times (resets ~21T22:00, 22T22:00, 23T20:00).
Exactly 3 OOMKilled restarts (exit code 137) are logged for notification-service: 2026-03-21T22:59:50Z, 2026-03-22T21:59:47Z, 2026-03-23T19:59:21Z; the cumulative restarts metric steps 0->1->2->3.

A full-scope change inventory over 2026-03-16 to 2026-03-23T23:59Z returns only dep-5402 (notification-service v3.8.0, 2026-03-21T00:00Z, 'Add in-memory template cache for email rendering', TemplateCache ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment, never rolled back) and dep-5415 (auth-service, unrelated).

Exactly one config change exists in the window across all services: cfg-2410 on kafka, log.retention.ms 604800000 -> 259200000 at 2026-03-23T18:00Z by platform-team; no memory-limit, consumer/batch, partition-count or replication-factor change exists anywhere.

The Kafka maintenance record cfg-2410 contains only the single log.retention.ms key change and documents no broker restart, no partition reassignment, no replication-factor/partition-count change, and no topic-level change; kafka deployment history in the incident window is empty (count:0).

notification-service memory_pct is flat/stable near the ~48% baseline for the entire observable pre-deploy day (2026-03-20T00:00Z through 2026-03-21T00:00Z, every 40-min bucket avg 46.75-50.08, latest 20-min bucket 46.0 avg / 46.79 max); the series is not already ramping before the deploy.

The first sustained monotonic upward ramp begins in the first full bucket after dep-5402: from the 03-21T00:00Z local minimum, nine consecutive strictly-increasing 40-min averages run 48.35 (00:40) to 58.97 (06:00); at 20-min resolution the ramp is visible from 00:20Z.

The post-deploy memory ramp is not accompanied by any CPU change: cpu_pct is flat at 24.38-25.34 avg across 2026-03-20T20:00Z-2026-03-21T06:00Z, with no step at the deploy or through the ramp — growth is not driven by increased processing throughput.

Old-gen heap pressure and long full GCs cluster in the ramp/peak windows (e.g. 'heap usage 8% over 90 (old gen), full GC took 4317ms' at 2026-03-21T21:37:01Z; 8220ms at 22:18:36Z; 10 WARNs between 2026-03-23T18:34:46Z and 19:49:28Z with 1646-6488ms pauses); the heap-over-90 pattern is the top logged pattern (35 occurrences).

Each restart is immediately preceded by a very large but short-lived consumer_lag spike (avg 790-2273, max 14214-18138) against a normal baseline of ~55-65 avg / ~120 max, returning to ~58 within the next bucket.

No other service in the metric set exhibits a sawtooth ramp/reset: order-service is flat at ~59-60% avg (F11), settlement-service is flat across 48 2h buckets (49.15-50.75) with zero restarts and lag maxima two orders of magnitude lower (max 82) (F27/F29/F30/F31), and auth-service is flat at 51.16-53.17% with zero restarts (F32).

notification-service exposes no heap/old-gen metric (heap_pct returns not_found); its available metrics are exactly consumer_lag, cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts, so memory_pct cannot be decomposed into cache vs non-cache or old vs young gen.

The only descriptive information for dep-5402 is a two-item manifest (TemplateCache ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment; render path uses cache) with no diff, PR, commit, TTL/size-bound/eviction/max-entries field, or cardinality metadata; no code or artifact endpoint was reachable, and no cardinality/key-space breakdown for userSegment is exposed anywhere.

No memory-limit telemetry for notification-service is reachable and no memory-limit/resource/JVM config change is recorded for any service; deployment history for notification-service over 2026-03-01 to 03-24 contains only dep-5402.
notification-service's metric data begins only at 2026-03-20T00:00Z and the earliest log match is 2026-03-21T03:00:44Z, so the week's earlier memory history (2026-03-16 to 03-20) is not observable.
kafka exposes no consumer_lag metric (only cpu_pct, messages_in_per_s, under_replicated_partitions) and no memory_pct, so broker-side lag/throughput and broker memory could not be read.

The dependency graph enumerates kafka with two producers (order-service, payment-service) and two consumers (settlement-service, notification-service); reverse-direction queries from notification-service and kafka returned no edges, and no deployment or config change exists for any of those producer/sibling services in the window.

Both historical precedents on the OOMKilled/lag/delayed-email axis (HIST-104 2025-11-05, HIST-112 2026-02-03) have partition-reassignment/rebalance root causes, not OOM or memory leaks; cfg-2410's retention change is a topic-data-lifecycle operation that does not by itself reassign partitions or restart a broker.

Historical-leads search for an unbounded ConcurrentHashMap/template-cache precedent returns only HIST-107 (2025-12-09, 'Cold cache storm after redis failover'), a cache-miss storm rather than a cache-growth leak, so it does not corroborate the unbounded-TemplateCache mechanism.

assumptions: Assumption: the TemplateCache introduced by dep-5402 has no TTL, size bound, eviction policy or max-entries guard. Only a one-line deploy manifest exists and no code/diff/PR endpoint was reachable, so unbounded growth is inferred from the deploy description, not inspected (F14/F15).

Assumption: the userSegment key dimension is high-cardinality (per-user or per-request) rather than a small enum, so the key space can grow without limit. No cardinality or segment-set metadata is exposed anywhere (F16).

Assumption: notification-service's container memory limit was unchanged across the window, so the sawtooth reflects rising heap against a fixed threshold. No memory-limit telemetry or resource-spec change exists; this is answered only negatively from an exhaustive change inventory (F18/F19).

Assumption: the memory_pct ramp represents cache allocation in the application heap rather than ordinary JVM heap warm-up. No metric can decompose memory_pct into old-gen vs young-gen or cache vs non-cache (F24); warm-up is a competing benign explanation that cannot be excluded from metrics alone.

Assumption: the ~24h OOM cycle is confined to the observable window and did not already exist before dep-5402. Pre-03-20 data is unobservable (F12); the one full pre-deploy day that is visible is flat (F21).

Assumption: the large pre-restart consumer_lag spikes (F9) reflect restart-related backlog drain or symptom of the same cycle rather than an independent external cause of the OOM; the sub-hour ordering of lag spike vs heap peak vs OOMKill cannot be resolved from 2h buckets.

Assumption: the metric set returned (notification-service, order-service, settlement-service, auth-service, kafka) covers the relevant broker-sharing services; services outside this set were not checked.

Assumption: the recurring cycle's true trigger is the cache deploy rather than an unreachable out-of-scope driver (e.g. a cron-like bulk workload or upstream batch producer), based on the exhaustiveness of the change inventory (F1/F2/F35/F36).

timeline.event: Earliest available notification-service metric data (first memory_pct point 47.86); memory stays flat near the ~48% baseline for the entire day. Earliest logs would not appear until 03-21T03:00Z.

dep-5402 deployed: notification-service v3.8.0 by s.menon, 'Add in-memory template cache for email rendering' (TemplateCache ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment). This bucket is the local memory minimum (46.0 avg / 46.79 max at 20-min resolution), consistent with a restart/scale event at deploy time.

First sustained monotonic memory ramp begins in the bucket immediately after the deploy (visible from 00:20Z at 20-min resolution, first full strictly-rising bucket 00:40Z at 47.19->48.35), climbing unbroken to 58.97 by 06:00Z while cpu_pct stays flat at ~24.9%.
Old-gen heap pressure and long full GCs appear in the ramp/peak window: 'heap usage 8% over 90 (old gen), full GC took 4317ms'; a further 'full GC took 8220ms' at 22:18:36Z.
Huge short-lived consumer_lag spike in the 21T22:00 bucket (avg 2273, max 17162 vs normal ~55-65 avg) preceded by an abrupt memory reset to ~48% in the same interval.
First logged OOMKill: 'container notification-service-7d9f OOMKilled (exit code 137), restarting'; cumulative restarts steps 0->1.
Second cycle: consumer_lag spike (avg 790, max 17612) and abrupt memory reset to ~48% in the 22T20:00 bucket.
Second logged OOMKill (exit code 137); cumulative restarts steps 1->2, roughly 24h after the first.

cfg-2410 config change by platform-team: kafka log.retention.ms 604800000 -> 259200000 ('Kafka maintenance: reduce retention to 3 days'). The record documents no broker restart, partition reassignment, replication-factor, partition-count or topic-level change; kafka has no deployment record in this window. This change postdates two of the three OOMKills.
Third cycle peak: 10 old-gen/heap-over-90 full-GC WARNs between 18:34:46Z and 19:49:28Z with pauses 1646-6488ms; consumer_lag buckets spike (18:00 avg 810 max 18138; 20:00 avg 1543 max 14214).
Third logged OOMKill (exit code 137); cumulative restarts steps 2->3; memory resets to baseline ~48%.

Incident INC-004 reported (SEV-3) by on-call SRE: third OOM restart this week, trade-confirmation emails delayed ~25 min, initial hypothesis that the consumer is choking on a replay after today's Kafka maintenance.
End of window: settlement-service and auth-service confirmed flat with zero restarts and no ramp/reset, so notification-service is the only service in the metric set with a sawtooth memory pattern.

recommended_actions.action: Immediately raise/pin notification-service's container memory limit (or scale its replica count) so the pod survives a full 24h cycle without an exit-137 OOMKill, and add a temporary restart/crashloop alert on notification-service so delayed trade-confirmation emails are caught before the ~25-min customer-visible lag. This is a mitigation only, not a fix: memory_pct ramps ~5-6pp per 2h bucket to ~97-98% (F7) against an unchanged limit (F18/F19).
recommended_actions.rationale: Stops the recurring customer-visible email delay while the real fix is prepared; the sawtooth plus triple OOMKill (F7/F8) is the whole failure mode.

recommended_actions.action: Prepare a rollback of dep-5402 (notification-service back to the pre-v3.8.0 release) as the standing mitigation, to be executed if the next cycle begins ramping again after the memory limit is raised. Rollback is clean because dep-5402 has rolled_back_at null and no later notification-service deployment exists to complicate it (F1/F17).
recommended_actions.rationale: H1 names the dep-5402 cache as the origin; removing the change is the only change-specific mitigation available, and the process has precedent for reversible deploys.

recommended_actions.action: Fix the cache in code: add an explicit maximum size (e.g. bounded ConcurrentHashMap / Caffeine maximumSize + TTL) or scope the key to a bounded dimension instead of template+locale+userSegment, then redeploy. Verify by confirming max cache entries is a documented, enforced constant in the diff before merge.
recommended_actions.rationale: The deploy manifest describes an unbounded ConcurrentHashMap keyed by a possibly per-user/per-request dimension with no TTL/size/eviction field (F14/F15/F16); bounding the cache directly removes the H1 mechanism.

recommended_actions.action: Verify H1 on the next deploy by watching memory_pct over 24h: it should stay flat near ~48-50% with no ramp past ~60% and no reset, and restart count should stay at its current value. If a ramp resumes with the same slope but a bounded cache is in place, escalate and re-open the hypothesis set.
recommended_actions.rationale: Provides the post-fix falsification test for H1 rather than assuming the change worked; the current sawtooth is the unambiguous baseline to compare against (F7/F8/F21).

recommended_actions.action: Rule out H2 empirically before closing the incident: pull kafka messages_in_per_s for 2026-03-21T00:00Z to 2026-03-23T23:59Z and compare the three lag-spike windows (21T22:00, 22T20:00, 23T18:00-20:00) against baseline. Flat broker throughput supports H1; a discrete surge coincident with the spikes would revive the replay hypothesis. Note cfg-2410 at 03-23T18:00Z postdates two of the three OOMKills and records no broker restart or reassignment, so it cannot be the origin of the recurring cycle regardless of the throughput result.
recommended_actions.rationale: The one discriminating datum for H1 vs H2 was never retrieved (F13), and this is the cheapest remaining test of the reported 'choking on a replay' theory.

recommended_actions.action: Alert on cache/heap growth rather than only on OOMKill: add a derived signal from memory_pct slope (e.g. sustained rise > 5pp over 4h with flat cpu_pct) on notification-service, so the next growth episode pages before the container reaches ~97% (F7/F25).
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents recurrence of a silent multi-hour ramp that only became visible as OOMKilled restarts and delayed emails (F7/F8).

recommended_actions.action: Add heap-level observability to notification-service: expose heap/old-gen/GC metrics (heap_pct returned not_found; available metrics are only consumer_lag, cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts) plus cache size/entry-count gauges for TemplateCache, so unbounded-cache growth is directly observable instead of inferred.
recommended_actions.rationale: The absence of heap/old-gen and cache-cardinality telemetry is why H1's mechanism could not be proven (F16/F24) and is the key data gap for any future recurrence.

recommended_actions.action: Adopt a deployment policy requiring cache/cardinality metadata (TTL, max entries, key source) in the deploy manifest or an attached code diff, so cache-introducing changes like dep-5402 are reviewable for unbounded growth at deploy time.
recommended_actions.rationale: The one-line manifest for dep-5402 with no TTL/size-bound/eviction field is what forced the causal mechanism to be carried as an assumption (F14/F15).

data_gaps: No code/diff/PR/commit or artifact endpoint was reachable, so the TemplateCache's TTL, size bound, eviction policy and max-entries guard remain unverified; H1's unbounded-growth mechanism rests on the one-line deploy manifest (F14/F15).
No key-cardinality or segment-set metadata exists for the userSegment dimension, so cache entry count cannot be bounded and the high-cardinality contribution to memory growth is unquantified (F16).

notification-service exposes no heap/old-gen/GC metric (heap_pct not_found; metrics are only consumer_lag, cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts), so memory_pct cannot be decomposed into cache vs non-cache or old vs young gen, and the ramp cannot be distinguished from ordinary JVM warm-up by metrics alone (F24).

No container memory_limit telemetry exists and no memory-limit/resource/JVM config change is recorded for any service, so the OOM threshold's constancy across the window is established only negatively (F18/F19).

notification-service metric data begins only 2026-03-20T00Z and logs only 2026-03-21T03:00Z, so the week's earlier history and any pre-dep-5402 cycle are unobservable; only one full pre-deploy day is visible and it is flat (F12/F21).

kafka messages_in_per_s and under_replicated_partitions were never retrieved (tool budget exhausted), so no broker-side throughput or replication data point exists; the H1-vs-H2 discrimination on volume/replay remains unanswered (F13).

No broker maintenance runbook/ticket/ops-log endpoint was reachable and kafka deployment history is empty, so whether cfg-2410 involved a broker restart, partition reassignment or topic rewrite cannot be confirmed or refuted (F33/F34).

2h metric buckets are too coarse to order the sub-hour sequence of lag spike vs heap threshold vs OOMKill within each incident night, and F9's lag spikes are equally explicable as post-restart backlog drain, weakening their evidentiary weight for H1.

Scope checks cover only the services in the returned metric set (order-service, settlement-service, auth-service); other broker-sharing services outside that set were not checked, and the dependency graph exposed no producers or siblings except via the single forward query (F4/F37).
Historical-incident search used one query pattern and returned no OOM-specific precedent for notification-service, so prior OOMKilled precedents may exist unretrieved (F5/F20).
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Code review or a heap dump showing TemplateCache already has a TTL/size bound/eviction policy and is not the dominant allocator would remove H1's mechanism and push the conclusion to inconclusive, leaving the ramp unexplained.

Heap/old-gen or allocation profiling showing the post-deploy ramp is ordinary JVM warm-up that plateaus below the OOM threshold would invalidate the causal chain (memory_pct is the only available proxy today, F24).

Kafka messages_in_per_s showing discrete throughput surges exactly coincident with the 21T22:00, 22T20:00 and 23T18:00-23:20 lag spikes would revive H2's replay mechanism and shift the origin to the Kafka path (F13).

Any discovered change outside the inventoried window — a memory-limit reduction, node-pressure event, pre-03-20 or out-of-scope producer/batch workload — would reopen H3/H4/H5 and weaken H1 (F1/F2/F18/F35/F36).
Pre-03-20 memory data showing the sawtooth already cycling before dep-5402 would refute H1's onset claim and support the chronic pre-existing cycle H3 (F12/F21).

Evidence that the three consumer_lag spikes are the cause rather than a symptom (e.g. lag rising hours before each heap peak, with per-message memory growth) would invert the causal direction asserted for H1 (F9).

findings.statement: Full-scope change inventory for 2026-03-16→2026-03-23T23:59Z returns only 2 deployments across ALL services: dep-5402 notification-service v3.8.0 deployed 2026-03-21T00:00:00Z by s.menon, 'Add in-memory template cache for email rendering' (TemplateCache ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment), status live, rolled_back_at null; and dep-5415 auth-service v7.1.4 deployed 2026-03-22T13:00:00Z by ci-bot ('bump jackson'), status live. No rollbacks occurred.

findings.statement: Exactly one config change exists in the window across all services (and for service=kafka): cfg-2410, key `log.retention.ms`, old_value 604800000 → new_value 259200000, changed_at 2026-03-23T18:00:00Z by platform-team, described as 'Kafka maintenance: reduce retention to 3 days'. No memory-limit, consumer/batch, partition-count, or replication-factor config changes were returned.

notification-service's only declared dependency edges are to kafka (kind queue-consume) and to external email-provider; kafka is marked shared=true owned by platform-team, notification-service is non-shared owned by growth. No upstream callers of notification-service and no other consumers of kafka are declared in the dependency graph.

Reverse-direction dependency queries returned no edges: depth-2 upstream of notification-service yields only the node itself, and depth-2 downstream of kafka yields only kafka — i.e. the graph exposes no producer services feeding kafka and no siblings sharing the broker, so producers/replay source cannot be identified from the dependency graph.

Two historical precedents were returned for the symptom pattern 'OOMKilled / consumer lag / delayed emails': HIST-104 (2025-11-05) 'notification-service lag after Kafka broker rebalance' — symptoms consumer lag spike, delayed emails; root cause 'Partition reassignment caused consumer group rebalancing storm'; and HIST-112 (2026-02-03) 'Settlement consumer stalled after partition reassignment' (settlement-service+kafka) — 'Consumer lost partition assignment during broker maintenance'. Neither prior incident's recorded root cause is an OOM/memory leak.

refs.quote: Partition reassignment caused consumer group rebalancing storm

findings.statement: Timing note (inference): the only two change candidates straddle the window differently — dep-5402 (in-memory TemplateCache, deployed 03-21 00:00Z, never rolled back) precedes the reported third OOM, while the retention change cfg-2410 at 03-23 18:00Z is ~2h20m before the 20:20Z report. Historical leads point at partition reassignment rather than replay alone; these are competing hypotheses for the OOM trigger, not established causes.

findings.statement: notification-service memory_pct exhibits a repeating sawtooth over 2026-03-21 to 2026-03-23: baseline ~48-50%, a steady ramp of roughly +5-6 percentage points per 2h bucket up to ~97-98%, then an abrupt drop back to ~48%, repeated three times (resets ~21T22:00, 22T22:00, 23T20:00).

Exactly 3 OOMKilled restarts are logged for notification-service in the window: 'container notification-service-7d9f OOMKilled (exit code 137), restarting' at 2026-03-21T22:59:50Z, 2026-03-22T21:59:47Z and 2026-03-23T19:59:21Z; the cumulative restarts metric steps 0->1 (21T22:00), ->2 (22T22:00), ->3 (23T20:00).

Each restart is immediately preceded by a very large but short-lived consumer_lag spike: normal buckets average ~55-65 messages (max ~120), whereas 21T22:00 avg=2273 max=17162, 22T20:00 avg=790 max=17612, 23T18:00 avg=810 max=18138, 23T20:00 avg=1543 max=14214 — returning to ~58 within the next bucket.

Old-gen heap pressure and long full GCs cluster in the ramp/peak windows: e.g. 'heap usage 8% over 90 (old gen), full GC took 4317ms' at 2026-03-21T21:37:01Z, 'full GC took 8220ms' at 22:18:36Z, and 10 such WARNs between 2026-03-23T18:34:46Z and 19:49:28Z with pauses 1646-6488ms; the heap-over-90 pattern is the top logged pattern (35 occurrences).

findings.statement: No memory anomaly in the only sharing-broker neighbor checked: order-service memory_pct is flat at ~59-60% avg / 64-67% max across 2026-03-20 to 2026-03-23 with no ramp or reset (restart not observed in its metrics window).

Metric data for notification-service only begins at 2026-03-20T00:00:00Z (first point 47.86) and the earliest log match is 2026-03-21T03:00:44Z, so the week's earlier memory history (2026-03-16 to 03-20) is not observable in the returned data.
The kafka component does not expose consumer_lag; its available metrics are only cpu_pct, messages_in_per_s and under_replicated_partitions, so broker-side lag/throughput could not be read.

The only descriptive information available for dep-5402 is a two-item manifest: "TemplateCache (ConcurrentHashMap) keyed by template+locale+userSegment" and "render path uses cache"; no diff, PR, commit, code, TTL/size-bound/eviction/max-entries field, or cache-cardinality metadata is returned by the deployment record.

No code/PR/commit or artifact-detail endpoint was available to the dependency toolset, so the question 'does the TemplateCache have a TTL, size bound, eviction policy or max-entries guard' remains unanswered by tool data (the summary line is silent on all of these).

findings.statement: notification-service memory_pct is flat/stable near the ~48% baseline from 2026-03-20T00:00Z through 2026-03-21T00:00Z: every 40-min bucket avg sits in 46.75-50.08 (max 46.79-54.77) with no trend, and the 20-min zoom over 2026-03-20T20:00Z-2026-03-21T00:00Z oscillates in 47.03-50.61 ending at 46.0 avg / 46.79 max at exactly 2026-03-21T00:00Z. The series is NOT already ramping before the dep-5402 deploy.

The first sustained monotonic upward ramp begins in the first full bucket AFTER the deploy: averaging the 40-min series, 2026-03-21T00:40Z is the first bucket that starts a run of 9 consecutive strictly-increasing averages — 48.35 (00:40) → 49.73 (01:20) → 51.34 (02:00) → 52.62 (02:40) → 54.17 (03:20) → 55.40 (04:00) → 57.38 (04:40) → 58.67 (05:20) → 58.97 (06:00). At 20-min resolution the ramp is already visible earlier: 47.19 (00:20) → 47.85 (00:40) → 48.86 (01:00) → 49.21 (01:20) → 50.26 (01:40).

The 2026-03-21T00:00Z bucket itself is the local MINIMUM, not a rise: 46.6 avg / 47.52 max at 40-min resolution and 46.0 avg / 46.79 max at 20-min resolution — a transient ~1-2 pp dip (consistent with a container restart/scale event at deploy time) immediately followed by the ramp, so growth starts after the deploy, not at or before it.

No heap/old-gen specific metric exists to corroborate the ramp: query for metric 'heap_pct' returned error not_found with the service's full available metric list being exactly consumer_lag, cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts.

The post-deploy memory ramp is not accompanied by any CPU change: cpu_pct over 2026-03-20T20:00Z-2026-03-21T06:00Z is flat at 24.38-25.34 avg (first 25.34, last 24.84, mean 24.89) and shows no step at the 2026-03-21T00:00Z deploy or through the ramp to 06:00Z — memory grows while CPU stays constant, i.e. growth is not driven by increased processing/throughput.

Interpretation: within the requested 2026-03-20T00:00Z→2026-03-21T06:00Z window the memory series is flat at ~48% up to the 2026-03-21T00:00Z dep-5402 deploy and the first sustained monotonic ramp starts in the bucket immediately after it (first strictly-rising bucket 00:20Z at 20-min resolution / 00:40Z at 40-min resolution), with no growth underway beforehand — temporally consistent with dep-5402, though this window alone cannot distinguish a TemplateCache leak from ordinary post-restart heap warm-up.

settlement-service memory_pct is flat across 2026-03-20T00:00Z→2026-03-23T23:59Z: 48 buckets at 2h granularity all have avg in 49.15-50.75 (e.g. 49.97, 50.56, 50.14, ... 49.19, 49.54, 49.56), summary min 44.44 / max 56.06 / mean 49.99, with no monotonic multi-bucket ramp and no abrupt reset to a low baseline — i.e. NOT a sawtooth like notification-service (~48%→97-98%→~48%, F7).

Finest-granularity zoom on settlement-service around the cfg-2410 Kafka maintenance (2026-03-23T18:00Z) and the 20:20Z report time shows no ramp and no reset: at 20-min resolution over 2026-03-23T12:00Z→23:59Z every avg is in 47.77-51.74 (e.g. 18:00=48.17, 19:40=50.21, 20:00=47.77, 20:20=48.48, 21:20=51.74, 23:40=49.98), range across the whole 12h is only ~4 pp (min 45.4 / max 55.09).

At 95-min granularity across 2026-03-21T00:00Z→2026-03-23T05:50Z (i.e. spanning notification-service's first deploy and all three OOM cycles) settlement-service memory_pct averages stay in 48.72-50.86 with no upward trend and no drop-to-baseline (e.g. 49.05 → 49.74 → 49.79 → 50.39 → ... → 50.86 → 50.41 → 48.72); summary min 44.44 / max 56.06.

settlement-service had zero restarts in the window: the cumulative restarts metric is 0.0 avg / 0.0 max in all 48 2h buckets from 2026-03-20T00:00Z to 2026-03-23T22:00Z (summary first 0.0, last 0.0, max 0.0), versus notification-service's 0→1→2→3 OOMKilled steps (F8).

settlement-service consumer_lag shows no spike-to-thousands: 24 buckets at 4h granularity over the full window have avg 41.98-47.67 and max 60.39-82.06 (summary min 6.06, max 82.06, mean 44.47), with the highest max (82.06 at 2026-03-23T16:00Z) still two orders of magnitude below notification-service's spike maxima of 17162/17612/18138/14214 (F9).

The only other service returned in the metric set, auth-service, also shows no ramp/reset: memory_pct over 2026-03-20T00:00Z→2026-03-23T23:59Z stays at avg 51.16-53.17 across all 48 2h buckets (summary min 45.85 / max 59.27 / mean 51.99) and its cumulative restarts metric is 0.0 in every bucket — so no OTHER service in the metric set exhibits a sawtooth ramp/reset in the window.

The Kafka maintenance record cfg-2410 contains ONLY a single key change: `log.retention.ms` 604800000 -> 259200000 at 2026-03-23T18:00:00Z by platform-team, described as 'Kafka maintenance: reduce retention to 3 days'. It documents no broker restart, no partition reassignment, no replication-factor/partition-count change, and no topic-level (per-topic) change — the record is silent on mechanism, not merely lacking detail.

Deployment history for kafka over 2026-03-20T00:00Z -> 2026-03-24T00:00Z returns zero records (count:0). There is no broker deployment/restart recorded anywhere in the incident window, so H2/HIST-104/112's assumed broker restart or reassignment has no documentary basis in deployment history.

Full-scope deployment list over 2026-03-21T00:00Z -> 2026-03-24T00:00Z returns exactly 2 deployments across ALL services: dep-5402 notification-service v3.8.0 (2026-03-21T00:00:00Z, 'Add in-memory template cache for email rendering', rolled_back_at null) and dep-5415 auth-service v7.1.4 (2026-03-22T13:00:00Z, 'bump jackson', ci-bot). No kafka entry, no rollback.

Cross-service config-change history over 2026-03-20T00:00Z -> 2026-03-24T00:00Z (no service filter) still returns exactly one change, cfg-2410 on kafka. No memory-limit, consumer/batch, partition, replication, broker-restart or maintenance-window config record exists for platform-team or any service; the word 'maintenance' appears only in cfg-2410's free-text description.

kafka's declared dependency neighborhood is now enumerated: producers order-service -> kafka (queue-produce) and payment-service -> kafka (queue-produce); consumers settlement-service -> kafka (queue-consume) and notification-service -> kafka (queue-consume). So kafka has TWO consumer services and TWO producer services sharing the broker — a producer-side volume surge or the settlement consumer cannot be excluded as the lag source from the graph; kafka is shared=true owned by platform.

Historical-lead search on the broker-restart/partition-reassignment axis returns the same two precedents (HIST-104 2025-11-05, root cause 'Partition reassignment caused consumer group rebalancing storm'; HIST-112 2026-02-03, root cause 'Consumer lost partition assignment during broker maintenance'). Both are partition-reassignment/rebalance root causes, neither an OOM/memory leak — but critically, cfg-2410's retention change is a topic-data-lifecycle operation, which does NOT by itself reassign partitions or restart a broker, so these precedents' documented mechanism is not matched by any record in this window.
